swap.evidence: Products tried: a tool-hire shop's click-and-collect and a council bulky-waste collection booking. Surviving unchanged: the wordmark (stock wrench icon + name in bold body sans), the green-on-pale-grey palette, bordered 4px cards, identical icon thumbnails, the month calendar, the radio-card session picker, the summary-box confirm page. Bound to this product: only the copy (deposits, 'Open' sessions, volunteers, Mill Lane) and the Open tags in the calendar. With the name hidden, a reader knows it is a booking form for tools but not that it is a volunteer-run library.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a community service booking flow: light ground, one green or blue accent, bold sans headings, bordered white cards, native-looking controls, error summary pattern, generic icon thumbnails. Predicted opposite: dark or editorial 'artisan workshop' look with kraft textures and stencil type. The render matches the default element by element (ground, accent, cards, icons, type voice).

similar_prompt.evidence: Similar brief: 'online reservation for a community seed library / a toy library run by parents'. Predicted choices: green accent, single sans in bold, card grid with placeholder icon tiles, calendar picker, summary-and-confirm form. Overlap is near total; the only brief-driven choices are the green said to come from the membership card (not visible as such) and the session-aware calendar.

mode_fit: All surfaces are Operate (done is Read). Quiet, conventional structure is correct and no hero moment is expected. The shortfall is the identity floor, not missing expressiveness: the library's own material (the actual tools, the membership-card green as a recognisable mark, the session rhythm) is absent from the brand layer.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Zero detector hits confirms there are no catalogue tells; the generic verdict rests on missing identity, not on tells. Considered SLP-28 (green sole accent): hue ≈147°, just outside the 150–175° band, and DESIGN.md gives a reason (membership-card green), so it would not apply. No change to verdicts.

findings.title: Every tool card uses the same wrench placeholder instead of showing the tool
findings.description: On /, all ten cards show an identical wrench line icon on a pale green square where a thumbnail sits. It carries no information about the tool and is the dominant visual element of the first screen.
findings.impact: Members recognising 'the drill with two batteries' by sight get no help, and the page reads as a placeholder layout, which may lower trust that the library is real and current.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: real photographs of the library's own items (the stock is one of each), or remove the slot so names and availability lead.

findings.title: Brand identity is only the name in body type beside a stock icon
findings.description: The header wordmark is a generic wrench glyph plus 'Fernhill Tool Library' in the body sans bold; no element carries the library's own world (membership card, community-centre room, sessions) into the brand layer.
findings.impact: The 'neighbourly' attribute is carried by copy alone; returning members on a phone may not feel they are at their own library rather than any booking service.
findings.recommendation: Decide which element of the library's physical world becomes the identity floor (e.g. the membership-card green as a recognisable mark) and apply it on every surface.

findings.title: Tool names truncate at 375 so similar tools become indistinguishable
findings.description: At 375 the card names are cut with ellipses: both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', hiding 'two batteries' vs 'one battery'.
findings.impact: On phones, the main device, members may open the wrong drill; the distinguishing words are the ones lost.
findings.recommendation: Let names wrap on narrow widths; the card can grow.

findings.title: Search moves below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: At 375 (default and filters-open) the 'Search tools' field, Search button and filter toggle appear after the full tool list, near the footer, while at 1280 they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Phone users with a tool in mind may not find search without scrolling past the whole list; the primary action of the find surface falls out of the first view.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same source and visual order at every width so search precedes results.

findings.title: Basket sessions at 1280: one wide card over five cramped cards, latest date first
findings.description: The session radio cards break into one full-width card (Wed 28 Oct) followed by five narrow cards whose dates wrap across three lines; the list runs 28 Oct down to 10 Oct.
findings.impact: Reversed chronology and the broken grid make picking the soonest session harder to scan and look unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list that keeps each session on one or two lines, in date order.

findings.title: Day-chosen state shows a non-session Monday as the pick-up day
findings.description: On /tool.html day-chosen, the text reads 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October' and the Mo 12 cell is selected, although the copy says only Open days are library sessions.
findings.impact: A member may reserve for a day the desk is closed; the calendar's own signature (Open days) is undercut.
findings.recommendation: Verify against the live page whether non-session days are selectable; decide whether they should be.

findings.title: Details lists on the tool page use two different value-column offsets
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from values start at ~224px while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at ~180px, directly beneath.
findings.impact: The ragged column reads as two unrelated tables and undercuts 'careful'.
findings.recommendation: Use one shared label column for all detail rows.

findings.title: Filter panel uses a browser-default date input showing yyyy/mm/dd
findings.description: Filters-open at 375 shows an unthemed native date field with 'yyyy/mm/dd' placeholder and an unstyled native select, against the en-GB 'Saturday 17 October' format used everywhere else.
findings.impact: The date format clashes with the rest of the product and the controls look unfinished next to the themed inputs.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the filter should offer session days (as the calendar does) rather than a free date; theme the controls either way.

findings.title: 'Added to your basket' toast covers the calendar weekday header
findings.description: In the added state the dark toast sits over the 'We' column header of the calendar.
findings.impact: Hides part of the calendar the member is using; looks like a layering mistake.
findings.recommendation: Place feedback where it does not cover task content, e.g. near the action bar.

findings.title: Done page still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: The nav on /done.html reads 'Basket (1)' although the reservation is complete.
findings.impact: Members may think the reservation did not go through or the tool is still pending.
findings.recommendation: Verify live whether the basket clears; reflect the true state.

findings.title: Short pages stop short at 1280: empty band under footer and empty right half
findings.description: Basket and done at 1280 end with a grey band beneath the white footer; confirm, done and tool keep content in a ~610px column leaving the right half bare.
findings.impact: Desktop lunch-break users see an unfinished-looking page.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the page frame fills the viewport on short pages and how the wide layout uses its width.

findings.title: Dark theme: green availability badges lose their pill background
findings.description: In dark on /, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges render as plain green text while grey 'Available from Sat 17 Oct' badges keep a filled pill.
findings.impact: The badge component changes shape between states, weakening the comparison the uniform cards were meant to support.
findings.recommendation: Give the available badge a visible container in dark, matching the other state.

strengths: Copy speaks like the desk volunteer: concrete, brief, product-true ('returned when it comes back clean and working', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower').
One filled button per page and a well-formed error summary with field-linked messages in both themes.
The dark theme is composed (lighter cards on dark ground, lightened greens), not inverted.
The calendar's 'Open' tags / dots tie the date choice to the library's session rhythm.
keep: Keep the volunteer voice and the session-aware calendar; build identity from the library's world around them rather than replacing them.
